THE FIELD SHAPE IS `tasks_write_cases`' AND NOT `models_read_cases`', because this is a writer: `input` is the state BEFORE and `file` is the whole document AFTER, so a recording that went green while the config was being clobbered is not expressible here. `file` is the file's exact BYTES rather than a parsed object -- null when no file was left on disk at all -- because jq's two-space pretty-print with its trailing newline is what /aimi:setup-models reads back, and only bytes pin that. `tree` names every file left in the throwaway root, which is how the OpenCode cache sibling and the absence of a stray mktemp temp file stay visible. `input` is the whole rebuild recipe: `config` is the file's exact bytes (null when there is no file at all, which is a different case from an empty one), `host` is claudeCode (CLAUDECODE=1) or opencode (unset), `opencode_stub` is the script installed on PATH under the name `opencode` (null when the binary is ABSENT), `python3` and `jq` say whether that symlink was placed in the shim directory, and `readonly` chmods the config root to 0500 for the run. EVERY CASE BUILDS A THROWAWAY ROOT with AIMI_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at it and a shim PATH of symlinks rather than the developer's -- non-negotiable for this verb in a way it was not for the readers, because this one WRITES ~/.config/aimi/models.json and a case that leaked would destroy the developer's own model configuration. Three normalizations fire so two captures can be byte-identical, and they are: the root becomes /TMP, the mtime-derived cache filename becomes models-oc-cache-<MTIME>.txt, and mktemp's six random characters become models.json.<RANDOM>. With them, two consecutive full captures are byte-identical. THIRTEEN THINGS THE CAPTURE ITSELF EXPOSED, each pinned by a case rather than by a sentence. (1) THE MERGE IS ITSELF A REBUILD THAT HAPPENS TO PRESERVE ONE KEY, which is counter-intuitive and is the reason this block exists. The jq is `{schemaVersion: "2.0", categories: ((.categories // {}) + {($host_key): {...}})}`, so exactly three things are true at once: `categories.<other host>` SURVIVES (dm-outro-host-cc, dm-ambos-hosts-cc, dm-flags-outro-host-cc -- this is the 1.97.2 regression and the whole point); `schemaVersion` is force-written to "2.0" even over a document that said "1.0" (dm-schema-v1-cc, dm-flags-schema-v1-cc); and EVERY OTHER TOP-LEVEL KEY IS DISCARDED (dm-chave-desconhecida-cc, dm-flags-chave-desconhecida-cc -- `updatedAt` and `notes` do not come back). The current host's own sub-table is REPLACED wholesale rather than merged, so an extra key inside it does not survive either (dm-subtabela-com-chave-extra-cc). Widening any of this to a deep merge would be an unrequested behaviour change; narrowing it is 1.97.2 again. (2) D6, VERIFIED, PINNED -- AND THEN REPAIRED, so THREE OF THESE RECORDS MOVED. What the capture found: `set -euo pipefail` at aimi-cli.sh:2, `pipefail` propagating grep's exit 1, and a bare assignment to an already-declared local together aborted the verb the moment the host's model list contained no "haiku" -- exit 1, EMPTY stdout, EMPTY stderr, nothing written, and in one case a perfectly good config left untouched with no explanation. The three documented fallbacks that follow (first line, second line, last line) were unreachable dead code. Reachable only on an OpenCode host whose provider set omits haiku; Claude Code's list is the literal opus/sonnet/haiku. The commit after the port made `|| _x=""` out of each bare assignment, which is the smallest change that turns "no match" back into the empty string the next line already assumed, and dm-lista-sem-haiku-oc-stub, dm-lista-so-sonnet-oc-stub and dm-lista-sem-haiku-config-existente-oc-stub each now hold exit 0, the table the fallbacks describe, and the ordinary two-line epilogue. Those three entries were written out BY HAND from the rule -- fast = first line matching haiku else the FIRST line, balanced = first matching sonnet else the SECOND else the first, powerful = first matching opus else the LAST -- and the replay then had to agree with them. The other 57 are untouched; what the bash did is in this file's history and in that commit's diff. ONE SILENT FAILURE SURVIVES and is deliberately not repaired here: dm-flags-valor-ausente-cc, see (8), which belongs to the argument parser rather than to this rule. test_no_case_fails_silently_except_the_one_the_parser_owns is what keeps that list from growing again. (3) D7 HAS NO CASE HERE, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN FAKED -- and then it was driven anyway, and REFUTED. No case in this block can reach it: every one runs non-interactively with stdin on /dev/null, so `[ -t 0 ]` is false and the prompt block never executes at all. So a double quote, a backslash, a newline, a tab, all four at once, non-ASCII and three control characters all round-trip correctly through the bash (dm-flags-aspas-cc, dm-flags-barra-invertida-cc, dm-flags-newline-cc, dm-flags-tab-cc, dm-flags-todos-os-quatro-cc, dm-flags-nao-ascii-cc, dm-flags-controle-cc, dm-flags-outro-host-com-aspas-cc). They are here for the port's sake: they are what proves Python's json.dumps matches jq byte for byte, and they found the ONE character where it does not -- U+007F, which jq escapes as \u007f and json.dumps emits raw. The two genuinely unescaped printf-built JSON sites in this file are aimi-cli.sh:9892 and :9929, BOTH inside cmd_check_version (the story that named them predates a shift in line numbers and attributed one to cmd_prime_cache, which builds all of its output with `jq -n --arg`). They are the next slice's, not this one's, and no escaping repair was made here. (5) FOUR INPUTS ABORT AT jq's OWN EXIT 5 with jq's own message on stderr and the config untouched: a document that is an array (dm-documento-array-cc) or a string (dm-documento-string-cc), where `.categories` cannot be indexed, and a `.categories` that is a string, in both modes (dm-categories-string-cc, dm-flags-categories-string-cc), where a string and an object cannot be added. It is non-empty, so the merge branch is taken; `jq empty` accepts it; and jq's stream over it holds ZERO values, so the merge emits nothing and the file that gets written is "\n". Data loss that predates this port and is carried across it unchanged. (7) jq READS A STREAM, NOT ONE VALUE, here as everywhere else: a two-document config is merged TWICE and both results are written into models.json, leaving a file that is still two documents (dm-dois-documentos-cc). (8) TWO ARGUMENT SHAPES ANSWER NOTHING AT ALL. `--research` with no value exits 1 with BOTH STREAMS EMPTY (dm-flags-valor-ausente-cc), because the parser shifts twice on a flag whose value is missing and the second `shift` fails under set -e. A bare positional argument is silently ignored and the verb runs in default mode (dm-argumento-posicional-cc). Neither is repaired by this story. (9) THE WRITE FAILING LEAVES THE OLD CONFIG INTACT, which is what the mktemp-then-mv discipline is for: a read-only config directory exits 1 with mktemp's message and the pre-existing document byte-for-byte unchanged, in both modes (dm-diretorio-somente-leitura-cc, dm-flags-diretorio-somente-leitura-cc). No stray temp file is left behind -- `tree` says so. (10) check_jq STAYS. A host without jq gets "Error: jq is required but not installed." and exit 1 before anything is read (dm-jq-ausente-cc). Deleting the check as part of a port to Python would silently admit a jq-less host to a verb the rest of the file still refuses to serve. (11) THE python3 CASES RECORD WHAT A python3-LESS HOST SAW AT CAPTURE TIME, which is everything: this verb was pure bash and jq here, so hiding the interpreter changed nothing (dm-python3-ausente-cc, dm-flags-python3-ausente-cc). They are here so the port's crossing is measured against a real before-state instead of an assumption. Unlike the four readers, the writer does NOT degrade -- see KNOWN_DIVERGENCES_WRITE for what it does instead and why silence is the one answer a writer must not give. (12) NUMBERS CARRIED ACROSS FROM THE OTHER HOST'S TABLE ARE RENDERED BY jq, not echoed: 1e3 comes back as 1000 and 1.0 as 1 (dm-outro-host-com-numeros-cc). Two extremes are split into their own case because jq's double cannot hold them the way Python's int can (dm-outro-host-com-numeros-extremos-cc: 1e+22 and -0). (13) jq PARSES `NaN` AND PRINTS IT AS null (dm-nan-cc). Python's json parses it too and would write the bare token NaN, which is not JSON and which jq itself would then refuse to read -- so the port renders a non-finite double as null the way jq does, and this case is what says so.

_comment_version_cache: THE FOUR VERSION/CACHE VERBS -- version, check-version, cleanup-versions, prime-cache -- captured at 112d72f before a line of aimi-cli.sh moved. THIS BLOCK IS NOT A PORT'S BEFORE-PICTURE, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE HERE THAT IS NOT. All four verbs STAY Bash + jq; the decision and its reasons are written out in cmd_prime_cache's header comment, which is their normative home. What the corpus records is the before-picture of a FIX: the empty-glob abort (D2) and the `ls`-pipeline glob that carried it. THE FIELD SHAPE RECORDS A FILESYSTEM, not a stream, because cleanup-versions runs `rm -rf`: `tree_before` and `tree` are the whole throwaway root either side of the run, so no case can go green while a directory it never mentioned was deleted. `global_cli_path` and `state_cli_path` are the two files these verbs write, recorded as content rather than as presence -- null when absent, which is a different fact from empty. `input` is the whole rebuild recipe and test_version_cache.py's _build_root is the only thing that reads it, so capture and replay cannot drift apart. EVERY CASE BUILDS A THROWAWAY ROOT with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, AIMI_CONFIG_DIR, HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointed at it -- non-negotiable here in the way it was for models_write_cases and more so: a case that leaked the developer's real CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR would have cleanup-versions delete the plugin install running the suite. The capture host exports CLAUDECODE=1 and AIMI_PLUGIN_DIR for real, so the recipe sets both explicitly per case instead of inheriting either. Two consecutive full captures are byte-identical. NINE THINGS THE CAPTURE ITSELF EXPOSED, each pinned by a case rather than by a sentence. (1) D2, VERIFIED AND THEN FIXED -- the reason this block exists. cmd_check_version documents a {status: "unknown", message: "No installed version found"} branch and cmd_cleanup_versions a {removed: 0, kept: null} branch, and NEITHER HAD EVER BEEN EMITTED. `set -euo pipefail` at aimi-cli.sh:2, plus a helper that returned 1 on an empty glob, plus a bare `var=$(helper)` assignment that carries that status, aborted both verbs above their own handlers. Observable behaviour was exit 1, EMPTY stdout, EMPTY stderr and no cli-path written. Recorded that way in nine cases -- an empty plugins/cache (cv-cache-vazio-cc, clv-cache-vazio-cc), an absent one (cv-sem-diretorio-cache-cc, clv-sem-diretorio-cache-cc), an unreadable one (cv-cache-ilegivel-cc, clv-cache-ilegivel-cc), the same under --quiet (cv-quiet-cache-vazio-cc) and the two metacharacter cases whose caches are also empty -- and every one of them now answers its documented JSON at exit 0. They are named in test_version_cache.py's KNOWN_DIVERGENCES and nowhere else, which is what makes 'the fix touched only these' checkable rather than claimed. The exit status was 1 and not 2: an earlier note said 2, from before the glob moved behind a helper that swallows ls's own exit 2 and returns 1 instead. (2) D2 AND D12 WERE ONE DEFECT WHEN THIS STORY WAS PLANNED AND ARE NOT ONE ANY MORE, which is worth recording because the planning note says otherwise. prime-cache was said to survive the same empty glob ONLY because its nested `bash -c` inherited neither -e nor pipefail. That stopped being true at 7133927: it survives because of an explicit `|| resolved_path=""`, and the nested shell was already reduced to a fork. So the two verbs' aborts and prime-cache's survival were independent by capture time, and pc-cache-vazio-cc records prime-cache answering not_found at exit 0 on the very root where its two siblings died. (3) D12'S INJECTION WAS ALREADY CLOSED, measured rather than assumed. A CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR of `cfg";touch MARKER;ls "` was expanded by the outer shell into the inner `bash -c`'s program text and DID run the touch on the parent of 7133927 -- reproduced here, marker created, prime-cache still reporting not_found at exit 0. On the captured code it does not: that commit passed the directory as a POSITIONAL ARGUMENT to a single-quoted program. The three metacharacter cases stay as the permanent regression, and the array glob removed the nested shell entirely, so there is no longer a program text for a config dir to be interpolated into. (4) D11, VERIFIED. write_global_cli_cache refuses to persist a path under a `.worktrees/` segment because such a path vanishes on worktree cleanup and every later session then exits 127. The refusal is a match on the path STRING. A cache entry that is a SYMLINK into a worktree has no such segment in its own name, so it passes: cv-fix-simlink-worktrees-cc, clv-simlink-worktrees-cc and pc-simlink-worktrees-cc each record a global cli-path written to a path whose target is under .worktrees/ -- exactly the outcome the guard exists to prevent. (5) D8, VERIFIED. cmd_prime_cache's OpenCode branch compares `candidate` against the expression it was assigned from seven lines earlier, so the comparison is tautologically false and its error branch cannot execute. No case here reaches it and none can; pc-opencode-ok, pc-opencode-nao-executavel and pc-opencode-sem-script are the whole reachable surface of that branch. (6) D13, VERIFIED, and it is three behaviours rather than one. cmd_version's only guard is that plugin.json EXISTS, so `jq -r '.version'` then prints the literal string `null` at exit 0 for a document with no version key (ver-chave-ausente), pretty-prints a JSON object across four lines at exit 0 when the key is not a string (ver-nao-string), and exits 4 with jq's own parse error for malformed JSON (ver-json-malformado). Only the absent-file case answers in the CLI's own voice (ver-sem-plugin-json). (7) cleanup-versions KEEPS A MALFORMED VERSION DIRECTORY OVER A REAL ONE, and this is a finding the corpus produced rather than one it was asked to confirm. `sort -V` orders `nao-e-uma-versao` ABOVE `1.2.3`, so clv-versao-malformada-cc rm -rf's the genuine 1.2.3 install, keeps the junk directory and writes ITS path into the global cli-path -- the same class of data loss 7133927 fixed, reached by a different route. It is recorded and deliberately NOT repaired here: deciding what counts as a version directory is a policy with its own blast radius (a prerelease like 1.2.3-beta.1 is legitimately not N.N.N), and this slice's scope is the abort. The recording is what a later slice should act on. (8) THE TWO JSON SPELLINGS COEXIST AND MUST. `current` is printf-built and compact ({"status":"current"}), every other check-version answer is jq-built and pretty ({\n  "status": "missing"}), and test-aimi-cli-part1-core.sh asserts both spellings LITERALLY. Uniform JSON would be a test-breaking change, so cv-uma-versao-atual-cc and cv-uma-versao-sem-state-cc pin one spelling each. The same care applies to cv-uma-versao-obsoleta-cc, which exits 1 while emitting valid JSON: non-zero-with-valid-output is load-bearing and callers read the body anyway. (9) TWO FAILURES THAT LOOK LIKE SUCCESS, both pre-existing and both preserved. A version directory that cannot be removed produces a stderr warning and a `removed` count that does not include it, while the verb still exits 0 (clv-nao-removivel-cc). And write_global_cli_cache returns 0 when it REFUSES to write, which is why prime-cache reports an error only when the write genuinely fails (pc-aimi-config-somente-leitura-cc, carrying mktemp's message inside the JSON).

TEN THINGS THE CAPTURE ITSELF EXPOSED, recorded here so nobody has to rediscover them from 46 recordings by eye. (1) THE `[ -z "$non_terminal_phases" ] && continue` ARM IS REACHED BY EXACTLY ONE INPUT, and it is not the one the code reads as if it guards. aimi-cli.sh runs under `set -euo pipefail` and that assignment sits on its own line after a bare `local`, so a jq that FAILS takes the whole verb down before the test is ever evaluated: nine inputs exit 5 with EMPTY stderr and NOTHING on stdout -- not even the `[` the array would have started with -- because jq's message was swallowed by the 2>/dev/null on the assignment that ran it (la-rm-doc-true, la-rm-doc-numero, la-rm-doc-array, la-rm-doc-string, la-rm-phases-ausente, la-rm-phases-null, la-rm-phases-string, la-rm-phases-numero, la-rm-fase-nao-objeto). The arm fires only for a roadmap.json jq read successfully while printing no count at all, which is an EMPTY file: la-rm-vazio EXCLUDES the feature and says nothing. Same class as _comment_archive finding (5), reached through the other document. (2) `jq -e .` PASSES ON AN EMPTY FILE. jq-1.6 exits 0 over zero documents, so "the probe refused this document" and "this document is empty" are different states with OPPOSITE verdicts: a malformed roadmap.json INCLUDES the feature (la-rm-malformado) and an empty one EXCLUDES it (la-rm-vazio). A port that collapsed the two would flip one of them. (3) null AND false ARE NOT MALFORMED, THEY ARE FALSY. `jq -e` exits 1 when the last output is null or false, so la-rm-doc-null and la-rm-doc-false take the same include-anyway path a parse error takes, while la-rm-doc-true and la-rm-doc-numero are TRUTHY, enter the `if` and then die at `.phases`. jq counts 0 as truthy and Python counts it as falsy, which is why the port tests `is None` and `is False` rather than truthiness. (4) THE JOIN IS DOCUMENT ORDER, NEVER SORTED, and its separator is exactly ", ": la-rm-ordem-do-documento stores phase 3 before phase 1 and the warning reads "3, 1". (5) `(.id|tostring)` IS COMPACT. la-rm-id-array records `[1,2]` and la-rm-id-objeto `{"n":1}` -- no space after the comma, none after the colon. Python's default json.dumps writes `[1, 2]`, and _jq_raw, the helper any port here would reuse, carries that default: nothing had ever handed it an array or an object until this corpus did, and this recording is what names the difference. (6) AN ABSENT OR null id PRINTS THE WORD null (la-rm-id-ausente, la-rm-id-null), a string id prints as itself (la-rm-id-string), and a string id holding a NEWLINE puts a real newline in the warning (la-rm-id-com-newline). That last one is why the port hands the joined ids to bash as the last RAW field with the compact payload behind them: a value that can span lines cannot be read off a fixed line number. (7) A PHASE WITH NO status IS NON-TERMINAL AND NOT STUCK, so the feature is excluded with NOTHING on stderr (la-rm-fase-sem-status, la-rm-status-null) -- a silent exclusion the warning was written to prevent, and it only prevents it for verification_failed. "Completed" with a capital C is non-terminal too (la-rm-status-maiuscula): the comparison is exact equality and nothing normalizes it. (8) `.phases` MAY BE AN OBJECT AND AN ENTRY MAY BE null. `.[]` over an object yields its VALUES, so la-rm-phases-objeto is a genuine completed phase and la-rm-phases-objeto-pendente a genuine pending one; and `null | .status` is null in jq, so la-rm-fase-null counts as non-terminal and excludes the feature, where a NUMBER in the same position aborts the verb (la-rm-fase-nao-objeto). (9) THE CONTRACT GATE IS NOT ON THIS SIDE, AND THIS IS WHAT KEEPS IT THAT WAY. _roadmap_require_contracts refuses a pre-2.0 roadmap by name for every contract-READING verb; list-archivable reads only .phases[].status and never a creates/needs entry, so it is ungated -- the same rationale roadmap-eligible's own exemption records. la-rm-pre-2-0-completed and la-rm-pre-2-0-verification-failed are roadmapVersion 1.0 documents carrying the old single-string creates entry and are read normally, and la-rm-sem-roadmap-version has no roadmapVersion key at all. A verb that starts refusing them is a behaviour change, not a port. (10) A TWO-DOCUMENT roadmap.json IS INCLUDED, WITH BASH'S COMPLAINT THE ONLY TRACE. jq reads a stream and `-e` judges the LAST value, so the probe passes; the count then printed one line per document, `[` was handed "0\n1", reported "integer expression expected" and returned 2, which an `if` reads as FALSE. la-rm-dois-documentos is included although its second document holds a pending phase. Same class as archive-dois-documentos-um-aberto and la-dois-documentos, reached through the third implementation. AFTER THE PORT: 128 of the 138 field comparisons are identical, and every stdout in all 46 cases matched -- the JSON array, its order, and the empty `[]` form two commands branch on. The 10 that differ fall in the same two classes every block before this one recorded, and neither is a rule anyone wrote. _jq_raw was repaired in that same commit rather than at the call site, so finding (5) costs nothing: the two other callers that can reach a composite value put the result in a message too. (A) THE ENGINE'S OWN STATUS WITH NO MESSAGE AT ALL, exit and stderr in the nine aborts of finding (1): jq died at its own exit 5 with its message swallowed, and roadmap.py refuses at 1 with one line naming the verb, the file and the shape it could not read. Every one of the nine still stops the verb and still writes nothing to stdout, which is the half that matters: the verdict is the recording, the number and the silence were the engine's. (B) BASH'S COMPLAINT ABOUT ITS OWN COMPARISON, stderr only, in la-rm-dois-documentos: the port reads the file as one document, finds it unparseable and takes the same include-anyway path, so the feature is still INCLUDED at exit 0 with nothing on stderr. What is gone is a diagnostic that named no rule; what is preserved is the defect it accompanied. The list_archivable_roadmap_cases array itself is untouched by the port commit -- only this paragraph was appended -- so a reviewer can diff the two commits and see that the record predates the replacement.

_comment_command_block_jq: Captured by running the 37 jq invocations that OPEN A FILE inside commands/**/*.md's ```bash blocks (never in aimi-cli.sh -- these live in the command layer, executed literally by an agent, one block per shell) against a 26-fixture adversarial tasks.json corpus, BEFORE story 02-04 replace any of them with a call to a CLI verb. Like story_merge_cases and list_archivable_roadmap_cases, this must NEVER be regenerated from the verbs that replace these sites -- regenerating it would turn the evidence into a snapshot of whatever the replacement does today, which is the opposite of what a golden file is for. EXTRACTION, NOT TRANSCRIPTION. capture-command-block-jq.sh sources the exact same extract_blocks() awk mechanism test-command-blocks.sh uses (factored into scripts/lib/extract-command-blocks.sh so the two can never see a different set of blocks), then scripts/tests/capture_command_block_jq.py walks every extracted block looking for a `jq [flags] 'PROGRAM' [args]` call whose LAST positional token is a bare $VAR reference -- the only file-operand shape any real site in this tree uses. A call with no such trailing token reads stdin (almost always `printf '%s' "$var" | jq ...`) and is excluded: it never opens a file. No file:line pair here was hand-picked; each was found because the parser said so, and a later run of the same harness against a changed commands/ tree will find a different set. THE COUNT IS 37, NOT 38. The planning census (see this story's own `notes`) estimated 38 by a mixture of grep and hand reading; the extractor's actual, mechanical count is 37, and per this story's own AC that is the number recorded -- the extractor was not tuned to reach 38. The single-largest reason for the gap: three jq lines the census counted (execute.md around STORY_VERIFICATION_URL, near the Wave Execution Loop) sit inside a *pseudocode* fence (``` with no "bash" info-string, opened at execute.md:2446) describing what the loop conceptually does -- extract_blocks() correctly never extracts them, because they are not bash. The extractor also originally missed two genuine sites (execute.md:458's nested `$(printf ... | jq -r '.file')` operand and :1499's `--arg p "$GROUP_PROJECT"` call) because shlex, unlike bash, has no line-continuation rule for a trailing backslash-newline; both are recovered by stripping `\\\n` before tokenizing (the ORIGINAL text, continuation intact, is still what is recorded as each site's verbatim `expression`). DISTRIBUTION (recorded, machine-produced): execute.md=32, plan.md=1, references/container-execution.md=2, references/execution-mode.md=1, review.md=1. By question-group: branch-name=8, execution-mode=3, metadata-type=1, pending-count=2, project-grouping=7, split-group=8, verification-visual=8. This matches the qualitative shape the story's notes named -- execute.md dominant, plus container-execution.md (2), review.md (1), plan.md (1), execution-mode.md (1) -- with the count itself corrected by measurement rather than asserted from the plan. SEVEN QUESTION-GROUPS, EACH SHOWN TO DIFFER ACROSS THE CORPUS (not asserted in prose -- scripts/tests/test_command_block_jq.py computes the set of distinct (exit, shellValue) pairs per group from this very array and fails if any group collapses to one): branch-name (6 distinct answers), execution-mode (4), metadata-type (4), split-group (9), verification-visual (11), pending-count (4), project-grouping (10). TRAP 1, RECORDED NOT REASONED ABOUT. The `branchname-nonstring-array` fixture sets `metadata.branchName` to a 4-element JSON array. `jq -r '.metadata.branchName' "$AIMI_ROOT/$TASKS_PATH"` on it exits 0 and prints the array pretty-printed across 6 lines (`[`, one line per element, `]`); every branch-name site's case against this fixture records `shellLines: 6` -- a real bash variable assigned by `$(...)` from this exact call would hold a 6-line value, not a single branch name, which is exactly the shape a prior slice found turning one array-valued id into four separate lines inside a bash read loop. TRAP 2, RECORDED NOT REASONED ABOUT. Every site's case against the `malformed-document` fixture (deliberately truncated, unparseable JSON) was OBSERVED, not predicted: jq exits 4, prints its parse error to stderr (`parse error: Unfinished JSON term at EOF ...`), stdout is empty, and the resulting shell variable is empty. No `set -euo pipefail` is in play in the probe shell (these blocks run in the agent's own shell, one block per shell, exactly as they do in commands/) -- the invocation simply fails and the rest of whatever block it lived in would keep running with an empty variable, unless that block's own prose checks for it. site-008 (execute.md:1229, `(.metadata.splitGroup | type) == "object" and ...`, the anchor-candidate type gate) is the cleanest illustration of jq -e's three-way exit: 0 only against the two `splitgroup-present-*` fixtures (a well-formed marker), 1 against every other well-formed document (the boolean test evaluates false), 4 against `malformed-document` (a parse failure, not a false test) -- three genuinely different outcomes a naive "it either matches or it doesn't" reading would collapse to two. REPLAYABILITY. Every case in command_block_jq_cases carries its own `input` (the fixture's full tasks.json text, or the malformed text for that one fixture) alongside `expression`, `exit`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `shellValue` and `shellLines`, following story_merge_cases' precedent -- test_command_block_jq.py replays every one directly (write `input` to the path the site's own operand resolves to, given the same variable bindings, run `expression` in a bare `bash -c`, compare every field) rather than describing it. Two consecutive captures of this exact set are byte-identical: the only source of nondeterminism (each probe's throwaway root, a fresh mktemp directory every run) is normalized to the literal string /FIXTURE-ROOT in stdout/stderr/shellValue before recording, and the sites/cases arrays are sorted (file, line, expression; then site, fixture) rather than left in discovery order. NEVER TOUCHES THE REPOSITORY'S OWN .aimi/tasks. Every fixture lives under a throwaway mktemp root the capture process creates and removes; each probe's subprocess environment is built from scratch with only PATH and HOME (pointed at that same throwaway root) -- AIMI_PLUGIN_DIR and CLAUDECODE are absent because they were never put there, not because something unset them. RETIREMENT CONVENTION, FOR STORIES 02-05. A site whose read is replaced by a CLI verb call is never deleted from command_block_jq_sites and its cases in command_block_jq_cases are never touched -- the case is the evidence the replacement preserves behaviour, and deleting the site would strand it (test_every_case_references_a_known_site requires every case's `site` to still resolve). The retiring story instead adds a `retiredIn` field to that site object, valued with the story id that retired it (e.g. "US-002"), in the same commit that rewrites the command file -- never left for a later story to mark, the same rule command-blocks-baseline.txt already follows for its own rows. test_command_block_jq.py's two live-comparison tests (count and file distribution) then compare the live extractor against only the sites still carrying no `retiredIn` key, so the suite stays fully green at every story's own commit rather than red from 02 through 05: a site removed from commands/ without being marked `retiredIn` fails one of those tests, and marking one that is still live fails the other.
